questions.title: Read a wave graph
questions.prompt:
The graph shows a wave.
What are the amplitude and wavelength of the wave?

parts.prompt: What are the amplitude and wavelength?

options.feedback: Both measurements use half/double-cycle distances incorrectly.
6 cm is the peak-to-peak height. Amplitude starts at the centre line.
The height from the centre is 3 cm; adjacent crests are 40 cm apart.
20 cm is half a cycle. Measure from one crest to the next.

parts.correctFeedback: The height from the centre is 3 cm; adjacent crests are 40 cm apart.

questions.modelAnswer: The amplitude is 3 cm. The distance between two adjacent crests is 40 cm, so the wavelength is 40 cm.
generalFeedback: Amplitude is measured from equilibrium to a crest, not from trough to crest.
Wavelength is measured between neighbouring points in the same phase, such as two crests.
questions.hint: Identify the equilibrium line. Then find two neighbouring crests.
sources: J24 Q1(a); J17 Q10(a); SPEC A1.1
questions.accessibleDescription: Displacement-distance graph. Vertical axis in cm from -3 to +3; horizontal axis in cm from 0 to 60. Crests occur at 10 and 50 cm, trough at 30 cm.

questions.title: Describe a longitudinal wave

Complete the statements about the wave.

parts.prompt: The particles oscillate ___ to the direction of energy transfer.

options.feedback: Perpendicular describes a transverse wave.
The particles move backwards and forwards, not only towards the receiver.
Parallel means along the same line as the energy transfer.
The particles oscillate; they are not stationary.

parts.correctFeedback: Parallel means along the same line as the energy transfer.

parts.prompt: The wave contains compressions and ___.

options.feedback: Rarefactions are the more spread-out regions.
Reflection is a wave changing direction at a boundary.
Nodes belong to standing-wave patterns.
Refraction is a change associated with entering a different medium.

parts.correctFeedback: Rarefactions are the more spread-out regions.

questions.modelAnswer: The particles oscillate parallel to the direction of energy transfer. The wave contains compressions and rarefactions.

Particles move back and forth around their positions; they do not all travel to the receiver.
Rarefactions are regions where the air particles are more spread out. Refraction is a different phenomenon.
questions.hint: Consider how particles move relative to the direction the sound travels.

questions.title: Calculate an ultrasound wavelength
questions.prompt:

parts.correctFeedback: Your value is correct.

parts.prompt: Select the correct rearrangement.

options.feedback: Speed and frequency cannot be added to obtain a length.
Divide speed by frequency to find wavelength.
This gives the reciprocal of the required ratio.
Multiplication does not isolate wavelength.

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength in metres.
parts.correctFeedback: Your value is correct.

questions.title: Interpret two waves in phase
questions.prompt:
The graphs show two waves, X and Y, at the same position.
Each wave has an amplitude of 2 mm.
Use the graphs to answer the questions about the waves.

parts.prompt: What is the phase difference between X and Y?

options.feedback: The corresponding crests are aligned, rather than a quarter cycle apart.
The same time spacing between crests shows equal frequencies.
Corresponding crests and troughs occur at the same times, so the waves are in phase.
Antiphase would put a crest of one wave opposite a trough of the other.

parts.correctFeedback: Corresponding crests and troughs occur at the same times, so the waves are in phase.

parts.prompt: Which type of interference occurs when the waves overlap?

options.feedback: Complete cancellation needs equal amplitudes and opposite displacements.
The waves are in phase, so their displacements reinforce rather than oppose.
Waves superpose wherever they overlap.
The in-phase displacements reinforce each other.

parts.correctFeedback: The in-phase displacements reinforce each other.

parts.prompt: What is the amplitude of the resultant wave?

options.feedback: Add the equal in-phase amplitudes: 2 + 2 = 4 mm.
The original amplitude is 2 mm; superposition of these waves doubles it.
The waves reinforce each other, so the resultant is not zero.
Adding two 2 mm amplitudes gives 4 mm; 8 mm would be the peak-to-peak height.

parts.correctFeedback: Add the equal in-phase amplitudes: 2 + 2 = 4 mm.

questions.modelAnswer: The waves are in phase: their phase difference is 0°. Their displacements add, producing constructive interference. The resultant amplitude is 2 + 2 = 4 mm.
generalFeedback: The crests occur at the same times, so the waves are in phase.
In-phase displacements add: 2 + 2 = 4 mm.
questions.hint: Compare the times of corresponding crests before adding amplitudes.
sources: June 2023 Q1(b): wave-pair interpretation; guide p.100.
questions.accessibleDescription: Separate displacement-time traces X and Y have the same period and amplitude. Both have crests at 0.25 s and 1.25 s and reach 2 mm from equilibrium.

options.text: Their combined line positions match every mixture line.

options.text: These gases have the greatest number of electrons.

parts.correctFeedback: Match all mixture lines and check for unexplained lines.

parts.prompt: Which electron transition emits a photon?

options.text: An electron moves to a higher energy level.
options.feedback: Moving upwards requires energy absorption.

questions.title: Read a standing-wave pattern in a pipe
questions.prompt:
The diagram shows a standing sound wave in a pipe.
The pipe is open at one end and closed at the other.

parts.prompt: Which expression gives the length of the pipe L in terms of the wavelength λ?

options.feedback: The drawing shows three quarters of a wavelength.
Three quarter-wavelength sections fit inside the pipe.
The drawing contains three quarter-wavelength sections.
One half-wavelength would have the same type of node or antinode at both ends.

parts.correctFeedback: Three quarter-wavelength sections fit inside the pipe.

parts.prompt: Is the open end a displacement node or an antinode?

options.feedback: Air displacement is greatest at the open end.
A closed end has the displacement node.

parts.correctFeedback: Air displacement is greatest at the open end.

questions.modelAnswer: L = 3λ/4. The pattern contains three quarters of a wavelength. The open end is a displacement antinode, where the air vibrates with maximum amplitude.
generalFeedback: The pipe contains three quarter-wavelength sections.
At an open end the air has its greatest amplitude of vibration. At a closed end its displacement is zero.
questions.hint: Count the quarter-wavelength sections between a node and the next antinode.
questions.accessibleDescription: The pipe is open on the left and closed on the right. Displacement antinodes are at x = 0 and x = 2L/3. Displacement nodes are at x = L/3 and x = L.

questions.title: Calculate string tension and pitch
questions.prompt:
A string is fixed at both ends. Its length is 0.50 m and its mass per unit length, μ, is 0.0020 kg/m.
Waves travel along the string at 150 m/s.
Calculate the tension in the string and its fundamental frequency.
Use v = √(T/μ) and v = fλ.

parts.prompt: Select the rearrangement for tension.

options.feedback: This rearrangement reverses the required relationship.
Square the speed, then multiply by mass per unit length.
The speed must be squared.
Multiply by μ after squaring.

parts.correctFeedback: Square the speed, then multiply by mass per unit length.

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension.
parts.correctFeedback: Your value is correct.

parts.prompt: Determine the fundamental wavelength.
parts.correctFeedback: Your value is correct.
parts.incorrectFeedback: The length is half a wavelength, so double 0.50 m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the fundamental frequency.
parts.correctFeedback: Your value is correct.
parts.incorrectFeedback: Divide 150 m/s by the wavelength in metres.

questions.modelAnswer: T = v²μ = 150² × 0.0020 = 45 N. The string contains half a wavelength, so λ = 2 × 0.50 = 1.0 m. f = v/λ = 150/1.0 = 150 Hz.
generalFeedback: T = vμ forgets to square the speed.
μ is mass per metre of string, not the total mass.
In the fundamental mode, L is half a wavelength, not a full wavelength.
questions.hint: Square both sides of the tension equation. For the second calculation, identify the fraction of a wavelength between the fixed ends.
questions.accessibleDescription: The string is fixed at both ends, 0.50 m apart. At its fundamental frequency there is a node at each end and an antinode at the centre.

questions.title: Apply the inverse-square law
questions.prompt:
A transmitter emits radio waves.
At a distance of 3.0 m, the intensity of the waves is 0.072 W/m².
Calculate the intensity at a distance of 9.0 m.
Assume that the inverse-square law applies. Use I = k/r².

parts.prompt: Calculate k using the intensity at 3.0 m.
parts.correctFeedback: Your value is correct.

parts.prompt: Which expression gives the intensity at 9.0 m?

options.feedback: 9.0² = 81, so divide k by 81.
This reverses the inverse-square relationship.
Square the distance before dividing.
Increasing distance should reduce intensity.

parts.correctFeedback: 9.0² = 81, so divide k by 81.

parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity at 9.0 m.
parts.correctFeedback: Your value is correct.

questions.modelAnswer: k = 0.072 × 3.0² = 0.648 W. I = 0.648/9.0² = 0.648/81 = 0.0080 W/m². Tripling the distance reduces intensity by a factor of 9.
generalFeedback: Dividing by 9 instead of 81 misses the square on distance.
Intensity falls with distance under the stated model.
The ratio is (old distance/new distance)², so intensity becomes one ninth of its original value.
questions.hint: Find k from the first position. Square the second distance before dividing.

options.feedback: Both are electromagnetic waves; a higher speed does not explain these results.

options.text: Bluetooth gains energy in the plastic screen, increasing the strength of the signal.

options.text: Bluetooth uses radio waves that passed through this screen well enough for reception.
options.feedback: Yes: the radio signal remained usable through this particular material.

options.text: Use Bluetooth because its signal will pass through every material in the room.
options.feedback: The test supports a choice for this obstruction; it does not prove passage through every material.

options.text: Use Bluetooth because interruptions are likely and it worked better with an obstruction.
options.feedback: Yes: this links the test evidence to people regularly crossing the path.
